title: NYT Investigation: Fraud and Waste in Ukrainian Defense Procurement Go Unchecked as Implicated Contractors Win More Weapons Contracts
detail: A New York Times investigation published September 6, 2026 found that fraud and waste in Ukrainian defense procurement are going unchecked, with contractors implicated in misconduct continuing to receive further weapons contracts. The report raises serious questions about oversight mechanisms within Ukraine's defense acquisition system during the ongoing war with Russia, where procurement integrity is critical to sustaining military operations and maintaining Western donor confidence.

media.caption: NYT investigation into fraud and waste in Ukrainian defense procurement

title: Witkoff and Kushner Hold 'Substantive' Kyiv Talks With Zelensky; Zelensky Rejects Territorial Concessions
detail: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on September 6 for their first direct talks with President Zelensky, a day after meeting Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Zelensky and senior advisers met the envoys twice, with UK, French and German national security advisers joining a third session. Zelensky said the US had floated Ukraine withdrawing from unoccupied parts of Donetsk Oblast to create a demilitarized 'free economic zone,' a proposal he called unworkable, and said he was open to dropping Ukraine's NATO membership bid in exchange for binding Western security guarantees but rejected ceding territory to Russia. Witkoff called the discussions 'substantive' and 'important,' while Zelensky said afterward that the war would likely 'continue in winter' absent a breakthrough.

title: Ukrainian Drones Knock Out 77% of Ryazan Refinery's Crude Capacity, Strike Rostov Airfield
detail: Ukrainian FP-1 drones struck the Rosneft-owned Ryazan oil refinery on the morning of September 6, hitting the ELOU-AVT-6 and AVT-3 primary crude-distillation units — together accounting for more than 77% of the refinery's roughly 17-million-ton annual processing capacity — and starting a fire, according to Ukraine's General Staff and defense outlet Militarnyi. The strike occurred during the temporary pause on capital strikes tied to the Witkoff-Kushner shuttle diplomacy, underscoring that the truce applied only to Moscow and Kyiv. The same overnight operation also struck the Rostov-on-Don military airfield and three Russian air-defense assets.

media.caption: Fire reported at the Ryazan oil refinery after a Ukrainian drone strike, Sept. 6, 2026
